note: Comment Delete has no settings page (configure=null). All configuration is third-party settings stored on the comment field config entity (field.field.<entity>.<bundle>.<field>, key comment_delete: operation/visibility/label/message/mode/anonymize/default/time_limit/timer). Delete access is overridden via hook_comment_access using static + dynamically generated per-field permissions; deletion runs through the comment_delete.manager service with operations hard, hard_partial, soft. This site has comment fields node.comment_forum (bundle forum) and node.field_blog_comments (bundle blog_post); medium/hard cases are grounded in real third-party settings on those fields. Cleanup/reset unset the comment_delete third-party settings to restore the baseline (no comment_delete config on the field).

evals.prompt: The Drupal contrib module comment_delete lets you choose what happens to a comment's threaded replies when the comment is deleted. What are the delete operations it offers, and what does each do to the replies?
evals.expected_output: Three operations: hard (delete the comment and all its replies), hard_partial (delete the comment and move its replies up one thread level), and soft (delete the comment but keep its replies, by unsetting its field values or setting it unpublished).

evals.prompt: I installed comment_delete on Drupal 11 but there is no admin settings page for it. Where do I configure its behavior (allowed operations, soft-delete mode, time limit) and where are those settings stored?
evals.expected_output: There is no configure route. You configure it in the 'Comment Delete' section on each comment field's edit form; the values are stored as third-party settings on that comment field config entity (field.field.<entity>.<bundle>.<field> -> third_party_settings.comment_delete).

evals.prompt: In comment_delete, what is the difference between the 'delete own comment' and 'delete own comment anytime' permissions, and which field setting makes that distinction matter?
evals.expected_output: The 'anytime' variants ignore the field's delete time limit, while the non-anytime variants only allow deletion within the window. This matters when the comment field has time_limit enabled with a timer (seconds after creation).

evals.prompt: On this site the forum comment field (node.comment_forum) has been configured with comment_delete. Inspect the live field configuration and report which delete operation is set as the default selected operation.
evals.expected_output: The default operation is hard_partial: field.field.node.forum.comment_forum has third_party_settings.comment_delete.default = 'hard_partial'.

evals.prompt: On this site the blog comment field (node.field_blog_comments) has been configured with a comment_delete delete time limit. Inspect the live field configuration and report whether a time limit is enforced and how many seconds it is.
evals.expected_output: Yes, a time limit is enforced: third_party_settings.comment_delete.time_limit = true and timer = 3600 (seconds) on field.field.node.blog_post.field_blog_comments.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use comment_delete to enable the 'soft' delete operation (delete comment, keep replies) on the forum comment field, node.comment_forum. Apply the change to the live field configuration.
evals.expected_output: field.field.node.forum.comment_forum carries third_party_settings.comment_delete.operation with the 'soft' key selected (e.g. via FieldConfig::setThirdPartySetting('comment_delete','operation',['soft'=>'soft']) or the 'Comment Delete' section of the field edit form).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use comment_delete to configure the blog comment field (node.field_blog_comments) so comments can only be deleted within 600 seconds of creation. Apply the change to the live field configuration.
